paragraphs:
### Submodule Integration

The PR adds a new Git submodule for x86-simd-sort located at `numpy/core/src/npysort/x86-simd-sort`, sourced from `https://github.com/intel/x86-simd-sort`. This external library provides optimized AVX512 sorting implementations for both 16-bit and 64-bit data types, enabling the performance improvements documented in this PR.

### CI Pipeline Updates

Both the Unix (`azure-pipelines.yml`) and Windows (`azure-steps-windows.yml`) Azure Pipelines configurations were updated to include a new build step for fetching submodules. The added step runs `git submodule update --init` with the display name 'Fetch submodules' to ensure the x86-simd-sort library is available during the build process.

### Benchmark Suite Modifications

The benchmark file `benchmarks/benchmarks/bench_function_base.py` was modified to include `float16` in the list of tested data types for sorting operations. This addition allows performance testing of the new AVX512-ICL optimizations for 16-bit floating point numbers.

### Build System Changes

The meson build configuration (`numpy/core/meson.build`) received several important modifications:
1. Added support for a `disable-simd-optimizations` build option that sets the `-DNPY_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION` compiler flag when enabled
2. Added `compile_args: disable_simd_optimizations` to the `npy_core_dep` dependency declaration
3. Replaced the reference to `src/npysort/x86-qsort.dispatch.cpp` with `src/npysort/simd_qsort.dispatch.cpp` in the source file list

These changes ensure the AVX512 optimizations can be disabled when needed (for debugging or compatibility) while properly integrating the new SIMD-optimized sorting code into NumPy's build system.

paragraphs:
### Build System Dependencies

The introduction of the x86-simd-sort submodule creates a new external dependency that must be properly managed. Build systems now require network access during `git submodule update --init` to fetch the Intel sorting library. This could impact: offline builds, reproducibility in different environments, and CI pipeline execution times.

### Hardware Requirements

The AVX512 optimizations require specific CPU instruction sets: AVX512-SKX for 64-bit sorting and AVX512-ICL for 16-bit sorting. Systems without these instruction sets will not benefit from the performance improvements. While this doesn't break compatibility (the code should fall back to standard implementations), users with older hardware will not experience the documented speedups.

### Backward Compatibility

The changes appear to maintain backward compatibility through runtime detection of CPU capabilities. The build system modifications include a `disable-simd-optimizations` flag that can be used to completely disable AVX512 optimizations if needed for debugging or compatibility testing. The fallback to standard sorting implementations ensures functionality on all supported x86_64 systems.

### CI Pipeline Reliability

The addition of submodule fetching steps introduces potential points of failure in CI pipelines. Network issues during `git submodule update --init` could cause build failures. The PR addresses this by adding the fetch step to both Unix and Windows pipeline configurations, but the reliability impact should be monitored in production CI runs.
